subject: Service continuity plan and evidence packet for reserved pool stall - DeltaApps
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@deltaapps.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: API Reliability Team <reliability@deltaapps.com>
Date: 2028-11-02T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected reserved GPU pool stall impacting /api/generate

Connor —

We saw a sustained 60–90s tail latency spike and intermittent 5–10% error rate on our /api/generate traffic between 07:40 and 08:05 PT this morning. Traffic was routed to your reserved GPU pool (DLT-5312); our users experienced partial failures. We've pulled local traces and can share logs if useful.

Can you confirm: what happened, whether this is fully mitigated, and what short-term measures you'll take to ensure continuity for the rest of today? Also please share any evidence we can provide to our internal incident review.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Head of Platform Reliability
DeltaApps

[attachment: deltaapps_client_traces_20281102.tar.gz (text/x-gzip)]

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@deltaapps.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-02T09:01:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected reserved GPU pool stall impacting /api/generate

Olivia —

Thanks for the heads-up and for attaching the traces. We saw the same anomaly in our telemetry and immediately opened an ops incident (SRV-8742). Short answers first: (1) root cause is an allocator race during scale-up under a rare fragmentation pattern; (2) mitigation completed at 08:20 PT and traffic is stable now; (3) we will send a consolidated evidence packet and a proposed credit calculation within 48 hours.

Immediate actions taken (this morning):
- Forced rebalancing of the reserved pool to reclaim fragmented slots (08:02 PT).
- Temporarily increased warm standby nodes for DLT-5312 while the team validated allocator fixes (08:05–08:20 PT).
- Engaged runtime team to patch the allocator; hotfix deployed to the control-plane at 10:30 PT.

I'm looping in our on-call ops and the runtime lead so we can consolidate logs and customer-facing material. Marissa, Karthik — can you confirm the artifact list we'll provide and whether the hotfix commit is ready to include in the RCA?

Connor O'Brien
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0184

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@deltaapps.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-02T11:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected reserved GPU pool stall impacting /api/generate

Olivia —

Appreciate the quick signal. We've packaged the initial evidence bundle and attached it here for your incident review. The bundle contains:
- scheduler and allocator logs (07:30–08:40 PT)
- pool allocation snapshots showing fragmentation state
- controller events around the scale-up flow
- a short timeline and hypothesis summary (one page)

Attachment: deltaapps_pool_diag_20281102.zip (log bundle, 12MB)

High level timeline (concise):
- 07:38 PT: DeltaApps increased concurrent worker count following a deployment on your side; traffic pattern triggered high ephemeral slot allocations.
- 07:40 PT: Allocator entered a fragmented state; some requests faced increased scheduling latency.
- 08:02 PT: Ops forced pool rebalance; traffic stabilized gradually.
- 08:20 PT: External error rate returned to baseline; no data persistence impact identified.

Next steps for transparency:
1) We'll deliver a formal root-cause report with the hotfix diff and test evidence by EOD tomorrow (2028-11-03).
2) We'll include a proposed credit calculation for the impacted minute-window.
3) As an operational precaution, we're enabling a transient warm-standby increase policy (no cost to you) for two weeks to reduce the blast radius while the allocator patch rolls out across clusters.

If you want an immediate postmortem call, I'm available 12:30–13:30 PT today. Otherwise we'll send the full package tomorrow.

-Marissa
Sr. Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Olivia Chen <olivia@deltaapps.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: API Reliability Team <reliability@deltaapps.com>
Date: 2028-11-02T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected reserved GPU pool stall impacting /api/generate

Thanks Marissa — the bundle is helpful. Two quick asks from our review team: (1) can you include a minimal reproducible trace (server-side request id mapping to our client trace ids) so we can correlate events in our tooling; (2) please include the commit hash and rollout timeline for the allocator hotfix.

We'd also like the proposed credit calc included in the packet — we'll need that for our procurement and finance review.

Assuming you deliver the RCA + credit by tomorrow, we don't need an immediate call.

Olivia

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@deltaapps.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-03T17:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Service continuity plan and evidence packet for reserved pool stall - DeltaApps

Olivia —

Attached is our preliminary root-cause report and the hotfix commit metadata you requested. Highlights:
- Root cause: allocator race caused by concurrent ephemeral slot reclamation + delayed heartbeat under a particular fragmentation vector.
- Fix: control-plane patch to make reclamation idempotent and avoid double-claim during scale-up; unit + integration tests added.
- Rollout: hotfix committed (hash 9f3c2d1) and staged across control-plane canaries on 2028-11-02 (10:30–11:15 PT); wide rollout completed to east/west control-plane domains by 2028-11-03 16:20 PT.

Attachments: redwood_root_cause_report_8742.pdf, proposed_credit_calc_20281104.xlsx

Credit proposal (summary):
- Calculated exposure window: 07:40–08:20 PT (40 minutes) with an elevated error rate.
- Proposed good-faith credit: prorated platform credits equivalent to one hour of reserved-capacity fee for DLT-5312, plus waiver of two weeks of warm-standby charges while we complete validation.

We're open to adjusting the credit after your procurement review but wanted to present an initial offer so your finance team can start the internal process.

Karthik Iyer
Runtime & Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Service continuity plan and evidence packet for reserved pool stall - DeltaApps

Karthik / Marissa / Connor —

Thank you for the thorough packet and the proposed credit. The RCA and commit hash align with our internal correlation; the reproducible mapping was especially useful. Our procurement team has requested the credit proposal be formalized in a brief amendment (DocuSign) — copying finance for next steps.

Two follow-ups we've captured for action:
- We'll take you up on the two-week warm-standby increase. Please confirm the start date and any expected observability hooks we should monitor.
- We'll schedule a joint postmortem review with our SREs next Tuesday (2028-11-07) to walk through the RCA and lessons learned.

Appreciate the rapid response and the transparency. We'll proceed with the amendment and loop you into the DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Olivia Chen
Head of Platform Reliability, DeltaApps
